name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+39 partisan lean makes a Republican win structurally implausible
Incumbent Glenn Ivey has a large financial edge, with $855K raised and $483K on hand
Republican George McDermott shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: The district's D+39 lean, Ivey's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising position leave the Republican challenger without any visible path; markets price this near certain for Democrats. With no competitive polling or ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals alone justify a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Only a major unforeseen development involving the incumbent, such as a scandal or health issue, would put this race in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 4th District, centered in the Washington suburbs, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+39. Glenn Ivey, the incumbent Democrat, is seeking another term and enters the general election with a substantial financial advantage, having raised roughly $855,000 and holding about $483,000 in cash on hand.

His Republican opponent, George McDermott, shows no reported fundraising or outside backing, and a Green Party candidate also appears on the ballot, further fragmenting any opposition. Prediction markets price a Democratic victory at roughly 98 percent. No public polling targets this race, but the structural advantages here are overwhelming, and the outcome is not in serious doubt.
